title: Is the Lisboa Card worth it? The maths, day by day
summary: The Lisboa Card costs €31, €51 or €62. We set it against the real ticket prices of Jerónimos, Belém Tower, São Jorge Castle and Lisbon's transport, day by day.
answer: Yes, on any day you visit two of the big paid sights. Jerónimos (€18) and Belém Tower (€15) alone cost more than the €31 24-hour card, before transport. It is not worth it on a Monday, when those two are closed, on a walking day with one sight, or for Sintra, where the palaces are only 10 to 15% off.

body:
## What the card costs

Turismo de Lisboa, the city's tourism board, sells the Lisboa Card in three lengths. These prices are valid until 31 March 2027:

| Card | Adult (15+) | Child (4 to 15) |
|---|---|---|
| 24 hours | €31 | €21 |
| 48 hours | €51 | €28 |
| 72 hours | €62 | €35 |

The clock starts the **first time you use the card at a public transport validator**, not when you buy it or collect it.

## What it covers, and what it only discounts

The card's official services list for 2026–27 makes these **free**:

- **Jerónimos Monastery** and **Belém Tower**: both need a timed slot (see below).
- **São Jorge Castle**, except for ages 13 to 15, who need a ticket.
- The **Royal Treasury Museum**, the **National Coach Museum** and the **National Pantheon**.
- **Public transport**: the Metro, Carris buses and trams (Tram 28 included), and CP suburban trains, which covers the lines to **Sintra** and **Cascais**.

What it does **not** make free:

- **Sintra's palaces** give a discount only: 10% at Pena Palace and Park and at the Sintra National Palace, 15% at the Moorish Castle, Monserrate and Capuchos. You show the card at the ticket office and pay the difference.
- The **ferries across the Tagus** are not included.
- The **Santa Justa Elevator** is on the free list, but both the card's shop page and Carris, which runs it, list it as temporarily closed.
- Several museums on the list are **closed for restoration**, among them the National Tile Museum and the National Museum of Ancient Art.

## What the same sights cost without it

Adult tickets, from each monument's own operator:

| Sight | Adult ticket |
|---|---|
| Jerónimos Monastery | €18 |
| São Jorge Castle | €17 |
| Belém Tower | €15 |
| National Coach Museum | €15 |
| Royal Treasury Museum | €11 |
| National Pantheon | €10 |

And for transport, from Carris and the Metro:

| Ticket | Price |
|---|---|
| One Carris/Metro trip on a Navegante card | €1.90 (valid 60 min) |
| 24 hours of Carris and Metro | €7.25 |
| A tram fare bought on board | €3.30 |
| CP return, Lisbon to Sintra (or to Cascais) | €5.10 |

The reusable Navegante card that the €1.90 and 24-hour fares load onto costs €0.50.

## The break-even, day by day

**A Belém day on a 24-hour card (€31).** Jerónimos (€18) plus Belém Tower (€15) already comes to €33, so those two alone pay for the card. Add the Coach Museum (€15) and a day of transport (€7.25) and the same day costs **€55.25** without the card, against €31 with it.

**A castle and Baixa day on a 24-hour card (€31).** São Jorge Castle (€17), the Royal Treasury (€11) and a 24-hour transport ticket (€7.25) come to **€35.25**. The card still wins, but only by €4.25. Drop one of the two sights and it doesn't.

**Two days on a 48-hour card (€51).** Belém on day one (€48 in entries) and the castle, Royal Treasury and Pantheon on day two (€38), plus two days of transport (€14.50), total **€100.50** without the card. That is nearly twice the price of the card.

**Adding Sintra on a 72-hour card (€62).** The card covers the train to Sintra (a €5.10 return without it), but the palaces only drop by 10 to 15%. A Sintra day therefore adds little value to the card. If Sintra is the main event, compare the price of the palace tickets on their own.

## When it is not worth it

- **On a Monday.** Jerónimos and Belém Tower are closed on Mondays (and on 1 January, Easter Sunday, 1 May, 13 June and 25 December), and the Coach Museum also closes on Mondays. Starting a 24-hour card on a Monday wastes its biggest savings. The castle opens every day.
- **If you'll see one monument and walk.** Jerónimos (€18) plus a 24-hour transport ticket (€7.25) is €25.25, less than the €31 card.
- **For children under 13 at the state monuments.** Jerónimos, Belém Tower, the Coach Museum and the Pantheon are free for children up to 12. Young people aged 13 to 24 and visitors over 65 pay half price there. For a young child, a child card mostly buys transport.
- **If your trip is mostly Sintra.** See above: the card discounts the palaces, it doesn't pay for them.

## Timed slots at Jerónimos and Belém Tower

Of all the places on the card, only **Belém Tower and Jerónimos Monastery** need a slot reservation. Card holders book it **after collecting the card**: advance reservations are not possible. Entry also depends on the daily capacity set aside for card holders. In practice, go early in the day and have a plan B for the afternoon.

## How to buy and collect it

You buy the card online and receive a confirmation by email. You then show it at an **Ask Me Lisboa** desk to collect the physical card. There is no digital card, and you should arrive at least 30 minutes before the desk closes. The tourism board lists desks at the **Airport**, **Terreiro do Paço**, the **Lisboa Story Centre**, the **Cod Interpretive Centre**, **Pilar 7** and **Belém Tower**.

Resellers sell the same card. On the Tiqets listing we read on 29 October 2026, the 24-hour card started at €31.00, the same as the official price. Their voucher also has to be exchanged for the physical card at an Ask Me Lisboa desk.

## Our verdict

The Lisboa Card pays off on any day that includes **two of the big paid sights**, such as Jerónimos plus Belém Tower, or the castle plus the Royal Treasury, and some transport. It loses money on a Monday, on a walking day with one sight, and on a Sintra day. Plan which days you'll use it before you choose 24, 48 or 72 hours, and start it on a Tuesday to Sunday.
